content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses identify the sword primarily as the Word of God — a penetrating, discerning spiritual weapon (Eph 6:17; Heb 4:12; Rev 1:16; 19:15) — with well-established secondary senses of divine judgment/wrath, war/violence, civil governmental authority (Rom 13:4), and division brought by the gospel.","book_summary":"The book identifies the sword as the Word of God wielded by the Spirit to discern and execute judgment; also as war and the governing force that carries judgment out. It proceeds from Christ's mouth, takes peace from the earth (Rev 6:4), and guards the way (Gen 3:24), with Peace named as its opposite in the war sense.","consensus_core_identification":"The Word of God as a discerning, judging spiritual weapon; secondarily divine judgment, war, and governing authority depending on context.","book_core_identification":"The Word of God discerning and executing judgment; secondarily war and governing authority that carry judgment out.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None of substance. The book folds the consensus's leading alternatives (judgment, war, governing authority) into a single integrated definition rather than treating them as separate context-dependent senses, and adds the 'guards the way' function from Genesis 3:24, but every element it asserts appears in the consensus's primary or common alternative senses. It omits minor consensus senses (Mary's sorrow, martyrdom, gospel division), but omission of secondary alternatives does not narrow the core.","material_contradiction":"None. The book's Word-of-God core, its judgment function, its war sense (Rev 6:4), and its governmental sense (Rom 13:4) are all affirmed by the consensus responses.","rationale":"The book's central identification — the Word of God wielded to discern and execute judgment — is precisely the consensus primary meaning, including the discernment emphasis (Heb 4:12) and the judgment-executing sword from Christ's mouth (Rev 19:15, 21). Its two additional senses, war (Rev 6:4, the red horse taking peace from the earth) and governing force (Rom 13:4), are both listed as 'common' alternatives by every response. Presenting these as one composite entry rather than context-sorted alternatives is a difference of packaging, not of extension or referent. The 'guards the way' element (Gen 3:24) is also anticipated by Responses A and D. The 'opposite: Peace' note aligns naturally with Rev 6:4 and the Matthew 10:34 tradition the consensus cites.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book REFINES the consensus by merging what the consensus treats as distinct, context-dependent senses into a single unified symbol (Word, war, and government as one judgment-executing referent), and by asserting a specific 'guards the way' function; but since every asserted case falls squarely within consensus-recognized senses and no boundary is moved, this remains an immaterial difference in presentation.","confidence":"high"}
